**Finding: missing (TRANSITION) — preferred-level insert validated and submitted.**

What I checked:
- **§ 13 Term (p0078)** — only obliges *Client* to arrange a new name server (30 days) and new hosting environment (60 days), and confirms Client retains domain/Client Content ownership. No Vendor exit duty.
- **§ 14 Termination (p0079)** — services simply run to the end of the month following notice; no assistance period, no data export.
- **§ 10 Confidentiality (p0061–p0068)** — no return-or-destroy obligation at all, so the planner's suggested analogue does not exist.
- **§ 2–4 (License/Hosting/Support)** — backups (p0038) and real-time log access (p0037) are operational, not exit rights; nothing survives termination.
- **§ 24 survival (p0090)** — survives Sections 1 and 5–30, but there is no transition obligation to survive.
- Searches for transition/export/delete/destroy/machine-readable returned nothing.

Conclusion: the fallback (90 days' assistance + 30-day export) fails entirely, and silence risks the walk-away outcome of no data return. I inserted one paragraph into the termination section carrying only the six preferred elements — six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return of Client Content and other Client data in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion after return — using the agreement's own defined term "Client Content" to avoid an undefined "Customer Data" reference, and no new section number to avoid colliding with § 15.
